Current schedule is Mon-Wed-Fri, USA timezone.

Jason wakes up in a mysterious world of magic and monsters. He’ll face off against cannibals, cultists, wizards, monsters, and that’s just the first day. He’s going to need courage, he’s going to need wit and he’s going to need some magic powers of his own. But first, he’s going to need pants.

Follow Jason as he makes a place for himself in a world that is strange, yet sometimes strangely familiar. He’ll meet crime lords and aristocrats, gods and monsters on his path from would-be victim to heroic adventurer. At least, he tries to be heroic. It’s hard to be good when all your powers are evil.

Please note: I am Australian and this story is written in Australian English, so there will be less of the letter Z and more of the letter U.

This web novel is also available at Scribblehub.com

Overall

Excellent story that gets slightly bogged down

Reviewed at: Chapter 607: A Difficult Child
by Book Gremlin Saturday, April 16, 2022 9:28:30 PM

This story is quite good, and throughout all 600 some chapters I never forgot what was happening and why. In addition, the mechanics of the world make sense and are fleshed out enough to be interesting without being needlessly convoluted. However, this story is quite prone to being bogged down. This is a slow story and the main character likes to needlessly brood from time to time, especially in the earlier installments, which can bog down the pacing of the story. In addition, the main character does not fly through the various ranks, so be warned. 

In all, I enjoy the wit and writing of the story, however the plots can feel overly dragged out at points.

Overall

Starts great, gets boring later

Reviewed at: Chapter 267 (Volume II): A Better Pants Solution
by Onward15 Friday, December 17, 2021 12:35:05 PM

I loved how well this started, truly fun. The system is unique, and the progression matters and is impactful. Really liked it until 

Jason leaves the fantasy world. Then it's back to earth, and boring as all hell. The characters fall flat, nothing really happen, and the game elements almost vanish. It turns into a bit of a self-indulgent family drama. I don't care about these new characters at all, and the interesting fantasy world or game-progression elements aren't there to shore it all up. I think Jason'll go back to the other world, but until then it's not something I enjoy reading. I stopped at chapter 305 or so. 

 

The author has lots of talent, and displays flashes of brilliance. But needs more consistency, especially later. Tbf, this is a common problem with most authors: Book 1 is epic, then it's downhill from there. The problem with writing so many words, I imagine, is there's little time to reflect and refresh. 

Essentially, strong early game, mid game is a chore. Late game? I'll let you know if I ever get around to read-playing it. Which I probably will, after a break (and lots of skimming).

Author deserves support, has done a good job overall, just has some consistency issues. Characters could stand to be less Jason-culty, but it's not bad to read, most of the times. Thanks 👍

Overall

End of arc1, a worthy read. Downhill after.

Reviewed at: Chapter 444: Which One of Us is the Villain
by Juneau Tuesday, May 25, 2021 3:59:15 PM

Updated review.

I thoroughly enjoyed arc 1, which I scored as a 4 and not a 5 in my original review.

It was and still is some very simple things for me. Jason, the MC hasn't changed or grown at all. He is funny, witty but extremely snarky about it we assume as a defence mechanism for everything. But he just stays that way, all the time and the few people I know like that in real life are annoying to be around, to the point where, you stop being around them. But in this story no one seems to care. Updated comment on this, it seems in later arcs everyone is turning into Jason. All the characters are this way.

In Arc 1 some areas of the story got stuck in repeat, certain conversation points were played out over and over, the comments section certainly got tired if it half way through.

And the big bad? There isnt one really. You have this concept of overwhelming power, unless it's against Jason then plot armour wins out. The story is missing the bad, in bad people.

Jason is always going to win, even when you know he shouldnt.

But it's fun. Enjoyed it all even though it's far from perfect.

After this, the Reaper trials were ok, more of the same and then we get to Earth. I was utterly stoked and excited to get to Earth and now were here, I'll be happy to leave. 

3.5 stars seems like its generous but it's still a fun read, if you can get over the whining, the same gimmicks and politics everywhere.

There is no payoff, no progress just a repetition of the previous chapters in a lot of ways and then when people die.

I didnt care, because I had no reason to. It's starting to lose it's way a bit and I'm hoping that this arc ends sooner rather then later in hope that the next arc is more like the first which was good!

Solid story but possible Deal breaker Intervals

Reviewed at: Chapter 302: Hardline Position
by Noissar Wednesday, October 14, 2020 7:49:40 AM

The story ramp-ed up rather well till the 260s when the Interval chapters appears.

I was really off put by the Interval chapters and waited till they were done before continuing to read on; My main issue was the Overt META knowledge and suggested railroad potential into a realm that felt like a Corruption of the story. I really did not enjoy it and what was implied. 

There was a near VETO like after math on what was written, having shunted my own personal tastes to the - I find that it was nearly to informative in a certain direction; but I think if those chapters were reorganized taking the first few bits that seemingly outline a railroad like Plot point - tone down the invisible hand guidance portion and intersperse it into the other NON MC chapters.

Meaning that the other scenes remain more or less the same but they play out and then have a short bit that explains/covers the meeting that gives those injected in as small well timed flash backs.

The reason for my personal grief is that some parts scream puppeteer and give the vibe of a removal on the MC's Agency. 

I would even suggest ignoring the Intervals except the last few cause the return to an organic flow but could be missing context and could be better to skip altogether.

The Character growth after those is AMAZINGLY Human; the story either returns to its true form or as I believe it get substantially more in depth and improves greatly - but having read the Offshoot Interval ruin much a mystic; with the foreshadowing being to blatant.
